stepNotes.1: Barrel index.js re-exports service/credentials/identity-storage; routes.js registers ~50 /api/git endpoints via a memoized lazy loader; service.js (4169 lines) holds git binary resolution, path guards, status/diff, and the worktree subsystem.
stepNotes.2: Boundaries are filesystem credential/identity reads, spawned git child processes, request-controlled directory/path/hash/branch inputs, and path containment; the credential token never reaches an HTTP surface and identity files are written 0o600/0o700, while runWorktreeStartCommand is the highest-privilege by-design scripting surface.
stepNotes.3: Path containment enforced at every file-touching entry via validateRepositoryFilePaths/resolveRepositoryFilePath and re-checked after repo-relative resolution; hash-gated operations guarded by isValidCommitHash at both service and route layers; index mutations serialized per-repo; reset/remote/worktree removal have explicit guards.
stepNotes.4: getStatus light mode and bounded new-file stat batches (200 files, concurrency 12) plus a 30s remoteExistenceCache limit cheap polling; filterActiveRemoteBranches fans out ls-remote to every remote with no cache, a latent multi-remote latency risk but not a correctness defect.
stepNotes.5: Barrel and lazy route loader are clean, but routes.js duplicates the directory-required check ~40 times and leaks sshCommand parsing logic into the /api/git/set-identity handler; the worktree subsystem inside service.js is effectively its own module and would benefit from extraction but is coupled to shared helpers.
stepNotes.6: The four flagged empty catches are all best-effort chmod/rm permission hardening in identity-storage.js (lines 13, 26, 30, 34) and are acceptable to swallow; each needs an explanatory comment rather than a code change; no TODO/FIXME present.
stepNotes.7: credentials/identity-storage tests assert permission bits and no-preflight-existsSync invariants; routes.test.js covers only stage/unstage through a mock harness leaving ~45 endpoints untested; service.test.js is strong on reset/cherry-pick/revert/hash-validation but covers none of push, pull, merge/rebase, or the worktree lifecycle.
stepNotes.8: The single registered finding (Low, deferred) on the four empty catches is accurate; this pass re-read each site and confirmed the disposition; no new Critical or High accepted since token never reaches HTTP, path/hash/branch guards hold, and the multi-remote and route-parsing issues are performance/design notes.
stepNotes.9: Ran pnpm test of all four git test files from desktop/packages/web: 4 files passed, 53/53 tests green in 17.58s under vitest 4.1.9; next valuable step is a push missing-upstream integration test and a createWorktree/removeWorktree round-trip.
